PagerDuty Bot: PAGERDUTY ALERT — Incident RWI-2026-0422 triggered in #eng-oncall. symptom=streaming_p95_p99_slo_breach, metric=streaming_tail_latency, p95=1.5s (SLO 400ms), p99=3.2s. affected_shards=[gpu-7,gpu-2]. paging -> @Anika oncall
Anika: acked. I'm on it. seeing a big spike in kv_cache evictions starting 03:11 UTC. customers report streaming stalls / partial responses. linking charts: https://console.redwood/alerts/RWI-2026-0422 (logs + P95/P99)
Sam: joining. any recent deploys?
Anika: no code deploys in prod in last hour. infra autoscaler kicked a few nodes but nothing unusual. heap/kv-slab metrics show steady memory pressure and frequent slab compactions on gpu-7. suspect prefill-heavy workload is evicting decode caches -> tail latency.
Leo: seeing the same in traces: many requests hit a prefill path that writes large KV entries, then immediate decodes miss and block. prefill_count skyrocketed ~03:10.
InfraBot: CPU/GPU utilization: gpu-7 78%, gpu-2 74%. kv_cache_eviction_rate: +420% vs baseline. slab_fragmentation_ratio: 0.68. stream_stall_events: +310%.
Anika: mitigation options: 1) throttle prefill concurrency globally; 2) disable client-side prefill routing for heavy-tenants; 3) route new streaming requests to fallback model variant without prefill; 4) bump kv_slab_target temporarily to reduce evictions. prefer quick low-risk: throttle prefill + route heavy tenants to fallback.
Sam: agree. do we have a runtime flag to reduce prefill threads?
Leo: yes: /etc/redwood/runtime/conf.d/prefill.toml -> prefill.max_concurrency (default 64). will set to 8 for all serving nodes in region eu-west-1. command below to patch via k8s job:
```
kubectl -n redwood exec -it deploy/serving-configurator -- /bin/sh -c "apply-config --set prefill.max_concurrency=8 --selector region=eu-west-1"
```
Anika: initiating patch on eu-west-1 now. also creating routing rule to send tenants with high prefill rate to fallback model: rollout 100% for tenant list.
Sam: I'll prepare fallback route. what about ongoing streams that are already stalled? any way to flush KV or restart workers?
Leo: warm restart of serving workers on affected shards will clear ephemeral decode caches but will also drop active streams. prefer to avoid unless necessary. short-term we can increase stream-timeout and send keepalive heartbeat to clients to avoid broken UX.
InfraBot: applying config change: prefill.max_concurrency=8 -> in progress. rollout id: cfg-2026-0422-1.
Anika: config patch applied to 60% of nodes in eu-west-1. early telemetry: eviction rate down 35% on patched hosts, p95 trending from 1.5s -> 700ms on patched nodes.
Sam: routing rule applied for top-10 heavy tenants to fallback variant (no-prefill). starting at 03:22 UTC.
Leo: metrics update: overall p95 across region 1.1s, p99 2.4s. stream stall events down 48% in patched hosts. still seeing tail spikes on gpu-2.
Anika: ok escalate to full region config if trend continues. preparing optional slab bump: kv_slab_target += 20% for affected shards — this requires a rolling restart of serving process. I'll hold unless p95 stays > 600ms after full rollout.
InfraBot: config rollout complete to 100% in eu-west-1 at 03:26 UTC. eviction rate across region now -52% vs peak.
Sam: oncall handoff: @Anika handing to @Sam at 03:30 UTC — I'll monitor for next 2h and coordinate with SRE to schedule any restarts if needed.
Anika: thanks. I'll create an incident channel and start a high-level blameless timeline + list of impacted customers. initial customer impact: 12 tenants experienced increased request latency, 4 tenants saw transient 5xx errors (stream timeouts). no data loss reported.
Leo: one note — prefill vs decode imbalance root cause: a recent customer workload pattern increased prefill writes of long prefix contexts which fragmented slabs. combined with continuous small decodes causing many small allocations, fragmentation reached critical threshold -> accelerated LRU eviction of decode entries.
Sam: action items captured: [1] Postmortem with timeline + root cause (owner: Sam). [2] Add preventive alert for slab_fragmentation_ratio > 0.6 (owner: Leo). [3] Add graceful prefill backoff in runtime (owner: Eng-ML). [4] Run eviction policy simulation in staging (owner: Eng-Platform).
Anika: incident status: mitigated (p95 under SLO target on patched hosts, region stable but monitoring for churn). will keep channel open for final verification and handoff notes.
InfraBot: incident RWI-2026-0422 status -> mitigated at 03:35 UTC. PagerDuty state: acknowledged -> resolved.
Sam: taking over. final observations: avoid slab bump unless necessary; software mitigations (prefill backoff + smarter slab allocator) are long-term fix. scheduling follow-up sync with Eng-ML and Eng-Platform tomorrow 10:00 UTC.
Anika: handing #eng-oncall to Sam. leaving notes in incident doc: https://confluence/redwood/incidents/RWI-2026-0422. Thanks all for fast responses :thumbsup:
Sam: thanks team. I'll collect logs/traces and prepare postmortem draft. closing thread once postmortem is published.
PagerDuty Bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: RWI-2026-0422 -> mitigated. Notifying customers: support will send out timeline and guidance.
Leo: quick reminder — add a regression test that models high-prefill small-decode workload to CI perf harness.
Sam: noted. closing handoff at 03:50 UTC.
Anika: thanks, closing from my side.
